claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
Controlled pre-oxidation can produce a thin, continuous, adherent Cr- and Al-rich oxide scale on this alloy.
The properties of the surface oxide scale govern degradation during elevated-temperature exposure.
A dense, continuous, adherent protective oxide scale suppresses inward oxygen transport.
Cr and Al promote formation of protective Cr- and Al-rich oxides at elevated temperature.
Al and Cr selectively oxidize on the surface of the specified Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti alloy.
Restricting oxygen ingress limits internal stresses and stress concentrations.
Restricting oxygen ingress mitigates microcrack initiation.
The engineered scale remains intact during oxidizing exposure at 750–900 °C for up to 100 hours.
An intact engineered oxide scale preserves fatigue performance during oxidizing exposure.
Reducing atmospheres destabilize the protective oxide scale.
Scale destabilization in 5% H2 in N2 allows increased oxygen penetration and localized subsurface oxidation.
Localized oxidation under reducing conditions causes microstructural degradation and microcracking.
Under oxidizing conditions, pre-oxidized samples will have fewer microcracks than mechanically polished samples.
Under oxidizing conditions, pre-oxidized samples will lose less fatigue performance than mechanically polished samples.
The protective benefit of pre-oxidation will be smaller in reducing gas than in oxidizing gas.
Mechanically polished reference samples develop a less controlled natural oxide layer.
At temperatures above 900 °C or times beyond 100 hours, extensive internal oxidation or diffusion-driven phase transformations may dominate degradation.
The controlled comparison uses pre-oxidized and mechanically polished specimens exposed at 750–900 °C for 10, 50, and 100 hours in either 21% O2 or 5% H2 in N2.
Failure of scale continuity or protective composition to correlate with improved degradation resistance would falsify the scale-governed mechanism.
